title: Directional whip-pan motion-blur cut
blurb: An ElementGL WebGL 2 canvas composites two live HTML scenes through a 16-tap directional velocity blur and RGB colour fringe with a damped overshoot spring, keeping buttons and editable inputs clickable at rest.
question: Can one ElementGL WebGL 2 canvas perform a directional whip-pan cut with 16-tap velocity blur, RGB fringe and a damped overshoot spring between two high-contrast HTML views while keeping both views clickable and editable at 0% and 100%?
result: Measured in HeadlessChrome/160.0.0.0 (2026-11-27): all 6 live checks pass at 412 px (DPR 2.625, 0.844 MP canvas, 6.75 MB initial, 12.18 MB peak, 0 errors) and 960 px desktop (DPR 2). Peak 50% directional smear drops edge trail luminance from 255 to 177 while reversing Left vs Up axes (Left H=97 vs V=12, Up V=84 vs H=12), and updateElementGeometry() routes real clicks and typing to View A at 0% and View B at 100%. Chrome 159 on Android and npm run check:jank stay not verified.
